provenance.origin: firm's own students pages: United States, London and Aberdeen
provenance.note: Three programmes with three separately stated eligibility rules. The Aberdeen page is the notable one: it states plainly that international students must already hold the right to work in the United Kingdom before employment starts, which is a stated position on work authorisation rather than silence. The London page carries a date inconsistency, left as found: applications are said to open on 1 December 2026 while responses are promised 'by the end of January 2026'. The CEP class-year sentence says the firm 'encourages' sophomores rather than requiring that year, so nothing is parsed from it. Sponsorship is silent on the London and United States pages although 'sponsor' occurs once on each: both are the site-navigation sector name 'Financial Sponsors', not immigration. The Aberdeen page is the only one that addresses work authorisation, and its statement is recorded as stated.
